issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies the attribute `numberOfTutors` as type `int`, but the solution declares `numberOfTutors` as `short`. This creates an inconsistent contract for the field type (and consequently for accessor/constructor signatures), which can confuse students and may break tests expecting `int`.
issues.suggestedFix: Use `int` for `numberOfTutors` in the solution (field declaration) to match the UML/problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a constructor that initializes all attributes in the UML order; since `numberOfTutors` is specified as `int` in the UML, students will implement `Lecture(..., int numberOfTutors)`. The solution instead defines the last constructor parameter as `short numberOfTutors`, creating a signature mismatch that can break tests expecting the `int`-typed constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor parameter `short numberOfTutors` to `int numberOfTutors` (and keep the parameter order matching the UML).

issues.description: The setter for `numberOfTutors` in the solution uses a `short` parameter (`setNumberOfTutors(short)`), while the UML/problem statement imply `numberOfTutors` is an `int` attribute and therefore the setter should accept an `int`. This mismatched setter signature can cause test failures if `setNumberOfTutors(int)` is expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Change `setNumberOfTutors(short numberOfTutors)` to `setNumberOfTutors(int numberOfTutors)` and store it in an `int` field.
